original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Resolve the explicit 15-call five-b weighted-tariff handoff (splits (6,5,4), (5,5,5), (4,5,6)) from PR #2314 and PR #2343 for diag([z],[uz],I_rest) over F2[UT4(F2)] across arbitrary finite restored dirty workspaces; expand the sharp price cone of the direct (4,6,4) word to beta <= 3 min(alpha,gamma) and prove cost 26 sharp (cost 25 impossible) at (alpha,beta,gamma) = (1,3,1).
scope_change_reason: Follows the second card method ('Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet') and resolves the explicit open handoff left by Gareth Davidson in PR #2314 and PR #2343 without starting a new native construction round. No physical conversion, new native alphabet or kappa improvement is claimed.
bottleneck_link: Scoped formal-model weighted lower-bound screen for the nonabelian UT4(F2) bit mechanism: proves that five b calls require at least 11 outer calls (L >= 16) across arbitrary restored dirty workspaces, eliminating all cost-25 15-call candidates at letter prices (1,3,1). Physical native conversion remains separate and the selected complex side remains binding.
stop_rule: Stop after proving two-role compression for (6,5,4) and (4,5,6), proving the three-role active-plus-dirty quotient decomposition for (5,5,5), and completing the exact 2-role and 3-role censuses for all three 15-call five-b splits.
evidence: Complete two-role quotient censuses expand 20,579,840 new 15-call words across (6,5,4), (5,5,5), and (4,5,6) (0 survivors), while reproducing all three predecessor domains (4,5,4), (5,5,4), and (4,5,5) byte-for-byte. Complete three-role quotient censuses for the two opposite-orientation (5,5,5) modes expand 42,447,616 words per mode (84,895,232 total, 0 survivors). Separate algebra, 3-role subsequence quotient, nilpotent same-label dirty compression, rank-sum profile characterization, and weighted price controls pass in controls.py.

open_questions.question: Does any realizing word with n_b = 5 exist at all in F2[UT4(F2)], or is n_b >= 6 an unconditional invariant for diag([z],[uz],I_rest) across all lengths L and role counts r?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Controls weighted optimality outside the cone beta <= 3 min(alpha,gamma), such as at (alpha,beta,gamma) = (1,4,1).
open_questions.first_step: Test whether an algebraic invariant in the 17-dimensional quotient Q rules out AC = 0 and ACB = I_2 simultaneously for every outer length when n_b = 5, or examine the 16-call splits (7,5,4), (6,5,5), (5,5,6), (4,5,7) (which also compress to at most 3 roles by PR #2343).
open_questions.blocked_by: No length-independent proof that n_b = 5 forces an incompatibility between AC = 0, ACB = I_2, and the 14 non-adjacent-{A,C} quotient equations is known yet.
